title: Jules operating card: verification blocked
summary: This intermediate resource explains why the Jules operating procedure cannot currently be used as verified guidance and identifies the evidence required to correct it. Product instructions are omitted because the previous source, replacement source, and existing guide content are UNKNOWN.
prerequisites: Network access for checking first-party product documentation
Version history showing the resource's previous source entry

sections.title: Can you use this operating card now?
paragraphs: No. An intermediate practitioner should not follow this card as product guidance until its source and procedure have been verified.

The only cited item supplied for this update is content/resources/coding-tools/jules-operating-card.json, described as having an unregistered publisher and never having been verified. Whether a cited web source moved or exceeded its review cadence is UNKNOWN because the existing object, former source URL, last verification date, and review cadence were not supplied.

The changed source therefore cannot be named accurately. Its former URL and replacement URL are UNKNOWN. This uncertainty affects every product-behavior claim, procedural action, recovery instruction, expected output, and verification method that depended on the missing citation, so those claims are omitted rather than asserted.
sections.callout: Stop here rather than treating an unverified operating procedure as current product guidance.

sections.title: Correction path
paragraphs: First, recover the complete committed contents and version history of content/resources/coding-tools/jules-operating-card.json. Preserve every unaffected field and paragraph. If the file or its history is unavailable, request the exact committed revision and do not reconstruct its contents from memory.

Second, identify the former HTTPS source and determine whether it redirected, was officially relocated, or merely passed its review cadence. If the former URL is absent from version history, record its identity as UNKNOWN and ask the resource owner for the prior citation instead of guessing.

Third, retrieve the current first-party documentation and compare each existing product claim and action with it. If the documentation cannot be opened, stop the review and arrange a network-enabled check. If a claim lacks first-party support, mark it UNKNOWN in the review record and omit it from the published procedure.

Finally, change only the citation and the material directly affected by the source review. If unaffected material cannot be distinguished because the original object is missing, do not publish a replacement object because doing so would destroy the correction-only diff.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is the original resource revision, the former source URL, evidence of a redirect or official relocation when movement triggered the update, the current first-party replacement URL, successful HTTPS retrieval, and a claim-by-claim record identifying what changed.

Verify the correction by comparing the updated object with the recovered committed revision. The diff should contain only the source correction, verification metadata, and paragraphs whose claims changed. If unrelated fields or paragraphs changed, restore them and repeat the comparison.

Verify completeness by confirming that every retained product claim has first-party support, every fallible procedure has a stated next action, and the final operating result has observable evidence. If any check fails, remove the unsupported instruction or return the resource for further research rather than publishing it.
